A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TLUE, with the same core benchmarks and evaluation framework. All 21 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v3, including appendices, tables, algorithms, and figures, support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v3 do not constitute missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs on Ti-MMLU and Ti-SafetyBench, including accuracy, response rates, and analyses of reasoning and model scale.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds translation-quality assessments, five-shot evaluations, uncertainty estimates, and qualitative and prompt-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The Claude translation, rule-based filtering, and expert-alignment pipeline remains substantively unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 retain the same answer-extraction procedures. The newly specified review rounds and expanded algorithm explanations document existing components rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The core coverage remains 11,528 Ti-MMLU questions across 67 subjects and 11,435 Ti-SafetyBench questions across seven categories, alongside the Chinese comparisons. Appendix A.3 adds an explicit translation-quality evaluation task for Google Translate and Claude outputs. The eighth safety category mentioned in A.2 has no corresponding reported evaluation.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain the same 13 LLMs and random baselines. v3 Table 2 adds Google Translate versus Claude-3.5-Sonnet for translation quality. Cross-language Tables 6–7 relabel older GPT and Qwen scores inconsistently with the retained prose, so these labels do not establish newly evaluated replacement models.

E3.justification: v3 supplements the retained zero-shot protocol with five-shot comparisons, four prompt variants, and translation-quality evaluation using BLEU, expert approval, and domain/cultural alignment scores. The reported curation team also changes from 15 annotators to five. These additions and reported revisions do not establish that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The resource-language, reasoning-model, and scaling analyses remain. v3 adds alignment-stage validation, five-shot sensitivity, prompt-wording checks, and worked cases examining knowledge errors, repetition, answer extraction, and non-monotonic scaling. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond v1.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run counts or uncertainty estimates. Appendix F and Table 18 in v3 first report 10 independent runs per model, standard deviations, and 95% confidence intervals for Ti-MMLU CAA accuracy. Seeds and interval construction remain unspecified; an increase from a known earlier run count cannot be established.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results, including Claude's 35.63 zero-shot versus 13.57 five-shot score and expert approval rising from 28.74% to 100% across alignment stages. Matched subject results also change: six CAA chinese_driving_rule cells differ, and DeepSeek-R1's world_religions DA score changes from 27.5 to 12.2. The old subject-table Average rows disappear. These changes do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version develops substantive theoretical results or proofs. The four extraction algorithms remain equivalent, and v3's additional metric explanations and empirical uncertainty reporting introduce no new formal derivation or mathematical property.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: TLUE is a large-scale Tibetan understanding and safety benchmark; current LLMs struggle; reasoning and scaling provide uneven benefits. Expanded wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting expert alignment to reduced translation artifacts, weaker models' five-shot gains to task misinterpretation, and stronger models' limited gains to linguistic limitations. It also discusses Claude's five-shot instruction-following failure and asserts prompt insensitivity. Appendices D and E give conflicting explanations of prompt misinterpretation. The original cultural-coverage limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 Table 5 supplies per-model temperature, top-p, and streaming settings, while Appendix C.1 identifies API execution platforms. Appendix A.3 discloses annotator authorship and two review rounds and revises staffing. The repository link changes from sun-shine to TLUE. These substantially expand reproducibility information, without proving changes to the underlying inference settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including the GPT-4 report, MMLU, BLEU, Sun-shine, TiSpell, and a low-resource machine-translation survey. The central positioning around Tibetan underrepresentation and adaptation of CMMLU and SafetyBench remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 separates Implementation from Performance, introduces numerous numbered subsections, and replaces the single appendix with Appendices A–I. It expands explanations of retained algorithms and datasets and rewrites the introduction and contribution statements. Author and affiliation text also changes. This is substantial reorganization beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the curation diagram, moves the overview into the appendix, merges the main result tables into side-by-side panels, and consolidates four subject tables into two. It redisplays the category mapping graphically and adds numerous case and validation displays. The response-rate bar charts disappear, while their underlying tabulated results remain.

improvement.justification: The added five-shot tests, curation checks, API settings, and worked examples address evidence and transparency gaps in v1. However, v3 introduces inconsistent model attributions in Tables 6–7, unexplained subject-score changes, and unclear confidence intervals: Claude's reported interval is 35.63 ± 2.35 despite a standard deviation of 1.20 and 10 runs. Conflicting failure explanations further weaken interpretation. These unresolved reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment that the additional evidence produces a net quality improvement.
